new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (48 pp., the PDF's metadata gives the title "PenDicIntroGram2020.docx", title page "(c) Ian Mackenzie, 2020", signed "Vancouver, February 2020"). extracted text of PDF p. 21 (printed p. 17, section "PENAN PHONOLOGY AND ORTHOGRAPHY") gives, as a stand-alone paragraph after the syllable-structure paragraph: "All syllables are equally stressed." — verbatim. PDF p. 42 (printed p. 38, "4.2 POSSIBLE STATUS AS CLITICS") gives: "However, they are not clitic-like insofar as they maintain complete prosodic autonomy from their "hosts"; all syllables in any Penan sentence are pronounced with an even, equal stress." — verbatim (reader's quote drops the leading "However,")., PDF p. 5 (printed p. 3…
new_statements.rule_in_words: According to Mackenzie, Eastern Penan has no word-level stress prominence: every syllable of a word (and of a sentence) carries even, equal stress; his 2012 orthography note states flatly that there is no stress. He adds that schwa can occur in a 'stressed' syllable and that final-syllable vowels are long in open syllables and short in closed ones, but he ties no prominence to that length.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (no primary stress is posited, so no secondary stress).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. The only prosodic qualifications are (i) final open-syllable vowels /a é i o u/ are long, closed-syllable vowels short, and final long vowels may carry an optional glottal creak; (ii) diphthongs and schwa do not take part in this length alternation.
new_statements.domain_note: Word and sentence level: 'all syllables in any Penan sentence' (p. 38) as well as the word-level phonology statement (p. 17). Impressionistic field description by a lexicographer-linguist (fieldwork since 1991), not instrumental; Mackenzie's dictionary is self-published, and his 2012 statement appeared in a peer-edited Festschrift. Sercombe's 2006 formal sketch, the peer-published description with a phonology section, could not be opened and may give a different (e.g. penultimate) analysis.
new_statements.identity_note: Mackenzie's dictionary and grammar describe Eastern Penan as spoken by the Penan of the upper Baram/Tutoh/Limbang area of Sarawak (principal informant Jokim; a few entries are marked "Tutoh" dialect); this is Eastern Penan proper (east2485), not Western Penan (west2563) or Penan Benalui. Sercombe's ELAR material is Sukang (Brunei) Eastern Penan, the same language.

sources.note: p. 17: 'All syllables are equally stressed.'; p. 38 (grammar sketch 4.2, on pronoun clitics): 'all syllables in any Penan sentence are pronounced with an even, equal stress.' Also notes p. 16 that schwa can be the vowel of a stressed syllable (unlike English) and that final vowels in open syllables are long, in closed syllables short.
